children.name: Ambient Clinical Scribes
children.blurb: Ambient clinical scribes are AI systems that capture audio from a patient encounter, usually in an exam room or telehealth visit, and produce a structured clinical note for the clinician's review.

children.name: Diagnosis and Billing Coding
children.blurb: Diagnosis and billing coding AI converts clinical conversations and documentation into structured diagnostic codes and billing codes.

children.name: Patient Record Summaries
children.blurb: Patient record summaries condense clinical notes, lab results, medications, allergies, and care plans into concise overviews for clinicians.

children.name: Clinical Decision Support
children.blurb: Clinical decision support in this part of the atlas covers software that turns clinical documentation and ambient conversation into structured suggestions, alerts, and documentation aids for clinicians.

children.name: Multilingual Intake and Triage
children.blurb: Multilingual intake and triage covers the automated capture, translation, and structuring of patient-reported symptoms, history, and demographic details at first contact with a health system.

sections.body: Clinical documentation and ambient intelligence is the part of medical AI that listens, reads, and writes alongside care. Ambient scribes capture a visit conversation and draft notes, while coding tools map notes to diagnosis and billing codes. Patient record summaries compress long histories into shorter views, and clinical decision support surfaces reminders, risk scores, or possible interactions. Multilingual intake and triage tools help collect symptoms and route patients when language differs. These systems are in active use in clinics and hospitals, but they are assistants, not autonomous authors of the medical record.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Speech recognition and note drafting are mature enough for routine use in many settings, though accuracy drops with accents, overlapping speech, and noisy rooms. Coding suggestions can speed billing, but they still need human review because errors affect claims and compliance. Summaries can miss rare but important details, and decision support can produce alerts that clinicians ignore or that reflect biased training data. The site tracks 1000 medical AI models, and this section is one part of that larger map. The honest limits are that none of these tools understand a patient the way a clinician does, and all of them depend on clean data, clear workflows, and accountable oversight.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the path of a clinical encounter, from first contact to final note. Ambient Clinical Scribes covers the listening and drafting step, where conversation becomes a note. Diagnosis and Billing Coding takes that note and examines how it becomes codes for payment and records. Patient Record Summaries looks at how long histories are condensed for quick review. Clinical Decision Support covers the prompts, scores, and checks that appear during care. Multilingual Intake and Triage handles the front door, where language and symptom collection shape who is seen and how soon, and together these pages show documentation as a chain of translation.
